- Subnational authorities have enhanced capacities to engage in holistic, area-based planning and consider different scenarios that respond to the needs of the host, refugee, and internally displaced persons (IDP) populations - Service delivery is increasingly responsive and generates more significant social stability outcomes based on the needs of the host, refugee, and IDP populations - Subnational authorities are empowered to facilitate local economic development (LED) and have better access to municipal investment that benefits the extension of safe public services and economic opportunities for the host, refugee, and IDP populations

In support of outcome 1: Subnational authorities have enhanced capacities to engage in holistic, area-based planning and consider different scenarios that respond to the needs of the host, refugee, and internally displaced persons (IDP) populations, in 2020, the Project started its engagement on capacity development of subnational authorities. Specific results are as follows: ? The assessment of the DGLAC was initiated ? Mediation units were established at UoM level and training of unit members was initiated ? An internal social stability strategy was developed ? The Bourj Hamoud Municipal hotline was established ? A detailed approach for municipal finance was finalized and a service provider to conduct the planned Municipal Finance Assessments was contracted ? Capacity development and training on raising revenues and financial management was initiated
In support of outcome 2: Service delivery is increasingly responsive and generates more significant social stability outcomes based on the needs of the host, refugee, and IDP populations, in 2020, the Project initiated its engagement on service delivery. Specific results are as follows: ? The assessment of the Regional Technical Offices (RTOs) was completed ? RTOs in Tyre and Al Fayaha’a were supported with grants ? Recruitment of RTO staff for the Bourj Hammoud Municipality and refurbishment of the RTO office for the Bourj Hammoud Municipality was initiated
In support of outcome 3. Subnational authorities are empowered to facilitate local economic development (LED) and have better access to municipal investment that benefits the extension of safe public services and economic opportunities for the host, refugee, and IDP populations, in 2020, specific results are as follows: ? The Project finalized a detailed concept note for its LED component ? The Project launched a procurement process for the planned LED assessments ? The Project launched the call for concept notes for basic service and LED projects for municipalities and UoMs and contracted a service provider to support municipalities and UoMs in this process through mentoring and coaching.
In addition to the above, the Project also further strengthened its M&E and communications work. In terms of M&E, in 2020, the project finalized its M&E framework, the baseline concept note in order to integrate the baseline in the project planned assessments, in addition to the M&E tools of the Social Stability component. In terms of communications and visibility, in 2020 the Project formally launched its activities in the three partner UoMs through a series of events. See section VIII Communication and Visibility for more information.

title.narrative: # Of Local Economic Development plans in the crisis context developed for the Unions of Municipalities.

description.narrative:
LED interventions supported by the project at Union level should be based on a local/strategic plan developed based on LED assessments.
The plan describes a LED vision for the area and explain the methods of addressing the needs in a relation to Basic Services and/or economic potential and available opportunities. The plan is an opportunity for the UOM to understand the economic structure under its jurisdiction and based on this understanding identify, prioritize the LED needs using the potential of the private sector and the community and propose the sequencing of addressing those needs through the development of the UoM economic potential.
This plan could be either an already existing document (e.g. Sustainable Development Plan) and the project team provides the technical support to the UOM to update and improve its economic component, or a newly developed document.

title.narrative: Number of Sub-national government structures are capacitated to plan and implement priority interventions

description.narrative:
Subnational government structure refers to the capacity of staff, council members and/or officials to efficiently and effectively implement municipal/UoM-related interventions.
This indicator measures the number of municipalities/Union of Municipalities that: - The staff and/or council members attended at least 75% of the capacity building and training events. - Showed 70% improvement in their skills and knowledge through the pre/post test. - Designed, implemented and maintained service delivery/LED projects.

title.narrative: # Of DGLAC staff trained on administrative and municipal-related topics.

description.narrative:
This indicator counts the number of Directorate General of Local Administrations and Councils staff trained on customer service for the automated call center, web portal and other municipal-related topics identified throughout the project.
Number of women will be proportional to total number of women of the DGLAC

description.narrative: This indicator counts the number of Lebanese and Refugees benefiting from jobs opportunities created as a result of the implemented Basic Services/LED interventions whether during the construction or the operational phase.

title.narrative: # Of vulnerable Lebanese and refugees benefitted from the implemented BS/LED projects.

description.narrative: This indicator counts the number of Lebanese and, IDPs and refugees impacted/benefitted directly/ indirectly through the implemented medium/large-scale projects.

title.narrative: # Of Operation and Maintenance plan developed for medium/large-scale basic services/LED interventions.

description.narrative:
This indicator counts the number of Operations and Maintenance plans developed for the implemented basic services interventions.
The Operation and Maintenance plans is covered with the existence of two documents; 1) a Business Development Plan (BDP) and 2) Operation and Maintenance Manual provided along with the delivery of equipment. However, some types of project such, irrigation, water and infrsustructre do not require Operation and Maintenance Manuals but only BDP. While, solar projects do not require the development of BDP, instead after sales services/warranty would be enough.

title.narrative: # Of subnational authorities staff/officials/RTO trained and coached on priority topics (sex disaggregated)

title.narrative: # Of subnational authorities with additional sources of local revenues

description.narrative: "Additional"means sources different than the main municipal revenue sources which are: taxes, leasing, IMF and donations (if available). This indicator counts the number of municipalities that implemented Basic Services interventions with LED aspect that according to the project proposal and the Memorandum of Understaning have the potential to generate revenues for the subnational authorities.

title.narrative: # Of vulnerable Lebanese and refugees benefitted from the implemented small-scale projects. (Sex disaggregated)

description.narrative:
"This indicator counts the number of Lebanese and, IDPs and refugees impacted/benefitted directly/ indirectly by the implemented small-scale interventions.
All people benefiting from the implemented interventions will be reported."

title.narrative: # Of implemented medium/large-scale basic services/LED interventions that are gender sensitive.

description.narrative: "This indicator counts the number of implemented interventions; that take into account gender issues of the communities during the identification and implementation of the interventions and plan to address them. Additionally, those interventions must consider the criteria of a gender-sensitive workplace (if applicable) which are: - paying equal wages and benefits - Setting fair hiring criteria that gives equal opportunity for all candidates (male/female). - Establishing an effective mechanism and reporting harassment. The interventions that meet the abovementioned criteria will be reported under this indicator."

title.narrative: # Of Medium/large-scale basic services/LED interventions implemented.

description.narrative: "This indicator counts the number of interventions established by the local authorities in or without the partnership of the private sector whose medium-scale interventions of around 450,000 USD each and are designed by municipalities with TA from the project but procured by the Project. The Project foresees a total of 3 large-scale projects of around 600 thousands USD each. "

title.narrative: # of Subnational authorities display improved and more transparent financial management practices

description.narrative: "This indicator counts the number of municipalities/ union of municipality that benefitted from the municipal solutions implementing by MERP project, which helps and leads to improving the transparency through resolving any discrepecnies reported in the financial statements and automation as well. Also, the provided solutions ensure sound financial management practices."

title.narrative: # Of small-scale basic services interventions implemented

description.narrative:
"This indicator counts the number of the designed and implemented small-scale interventions those whose budget don't exceed 50,000 USD each, designed by municipalities themselves are procured by MERP.
Small-scale projects provide basic services to the community, such as water, infrustructure, solar."
